### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **28** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/automation.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/automation.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**8** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx`  _(via record.amount (literal, a string literal in a comment on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/automation/connectors.mdx`  _(via connectorConfig (symbol, a field of const object FLOW_NODE_SIBLING_EXPRESSION_BLOCKS), connectorConfig (literal, a string literal in block), connector_action (literal, a string literal in connectorConfig; a string literal in nodeType))_

⛔ **9** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v15.mdx`  _(via connector_action (literal, a string literal in connectorConfig; a string literal in nodeType))_
- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via AutomationEngine (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via AutomationEngine (symbol, a top-level class), FlowSchema (symbol, a top-level const), connector_action (literal, a string literal in connectorConfig; a string literal in nodeType))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/automation.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/automation.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **6** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **58** of **210** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **168** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 93242324040563e9db96c98ef186948797d20cbd` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `73793eef54e49e47feea9bfb2d6c45561e6c48e6` — the merge of head `6a06a420b1c77e30d4aee538e531687fc4e0a7eb` into base `93242324040563e9db96c98ef186948797d20cbd`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 73793eef54e49e47feea9bfb2d6c45561e6c48e6 && git checkout 73793eef54e49e47feea9bfb2d6c45561e6c48e6
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 93242324040563e9db96c98ef186948797d20cbd 6a06a420b1c77e30d4aee538e531687fc4e0a7eb && git checkout -B drift-repro 93242324040563e9db96c98ef186948797d20cbd && git merge --no-ff 6a06a420b1c77e30d4aee538e531687fc4e0a7eb

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 93242324040563e9db96c98ef186948797d20cbd
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 93242324040563e9db96c98ef186948797d20cbd` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `6a06a420b1c77e30d4aee538e531687fc4e0a7eb`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/automation/flow-node-config-refusals.ts, packages/spec/src/automation/flow-node-expression-paths.ts, packages/spec/src/automation/flow-value-slot-template.ts, packages/spec/src/automation/flow.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.connector-action-input-value-slot-judged.ts + narrowing-face floor (every diff path outside the prose faces): packages/services/service-automation/src/flow-registration-checks.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/config-expression-ledger.test.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/connector-input-registration.test.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.connector-input.test.ts, packages/spec/src/automation/flow-node-expression-paths.test.ts, packages/spec/src/automation/flow-value-slot-template.test.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/runtime-authoring-gate.flow-credential-literal.test.ts, packages/cli/test/flow-credential-literal-doors.e2e.test.ts, examples/app-showcase/src/automation/flows/index.ts; cited code read on the head: packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/connector-nodes.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/value-slot-map.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/plugin.ts, packages/spec/src/automation/flow-sibling-block-loose-keys.ts, packages/spec/src/automation/flow-template-token.ts, packages/spec/src/conversions/refused-shapes.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/inspectors/flow-value-envelope.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/inspectors/FlowNodeConfigField.tsx, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/previews/simulator/flow-simulator.ts, skills/objectstack-automation/SKILL.md, skills/objectstack-automation/references/integration-recipes.md, the three `.changeset/27968-*.md`, AGENTS.md step 3, pm-dispatch SKILL.md `Skills-docs:` clause. Reviewed at 2026-10-30T14:42Z against the three-dot diff `27e0bd58...6a06a420` (merge-base `91a423ef`), card #27968 body + 4 comments, PR body + 22-file list, and the check-runs on the head.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Accept-set narrowing at `AutomationEngine.registerFlow`** — a `connector_action` node's `connectorConfig.input.KEY` holding (a) a malformed CEL envelope, (b) a template-dialect envelope, (c) a string carrying a single-brace `{…}` token anywhere in the value (a string inside a nested list or object included) is refused; the refusal is thrown (`engine.ts:4387` iterates `registrationChecks({ advisory: true })` and throws the first refusal — `advisory` there enables the logged schema pass, it does not soften the throw). **Right.** The judge is the shared one: `flowNodeValueTemplateRefusals(node.type, node.config, node)` and `resolveFlowNodeExpressions(node.type, node.config, node)` at `flow-registration-checks.ts:598/641`, the same two calls the `subflow` `config.input.*` row already takes, located as `BLOCK.PATH`. No second list, as triage 6487582764 / 6516097905 ruled.
2. **The same narrowing at `validateStackExpressions` (`objectstack validate`) and at the runtime authoring gate**, which runs the same pass (`validate-expressions.ts:2775/2834`; lint test asserts rule `expression-invalid` at the gate). **Right.** A valid envelope there is also held to the value slots' unbound-root judgment (`refuseUnboundRoots(…, 'value')`), as every value slot is; the lint changeset names it. **Right.**
3. **Boot reach** — a stored flow row carrying one of the three shapes is skipped with `[Automation] failed to register flow` (plugin.ts:1571, re-sync 3539, cold-boot bind 3616), the flows beside it register. **Right**; the D3 entry's acceptance criteria name that warn as the locator.
4. **Executor unchanged, one reject set** — `connector-nodes.ts:125` `resolveValueSlotMap(engine, cfg.input, …)` evaluates TOP-LEVEL envelopes and hands every other value on as a copy; the ledger row `input.*` emits top-level envelope-shaped values for the envelope check and the template judge walks nested strings for tokens — identical to `subflow.input.*`. A nested envelope (`body.filter`) is data at both doors and at the executor (registration test asserts the handler receives it verbatim). **Right.**
5. **The grammar the slot now takes** — `tokensOf` is `templateTokensOf` (`/\{([^{}]+)\}/g`), so every `{…}` is a token, an `unresolvable` one included (`refusalOf('{"a": 1}')` in the spec test is a refusal), and a `{{ x }}` hole is matched as the single-brace token `{ x }` and refused too. This is exactly what the 17.x interpolator substituted and exactly what `subflow.input` refuses today, so the entry's "a single-brace `{…}` token … anywhere in the value" is accurate. **Right by ruling**; see ④ for what it does to the recipe text.
6. **`FlowSchema.parse` byte-identical** — `connectorConfig.input` values stay `z.unknown()` (now `.meta({ xExpression: 'value' })`, a marker, not a refinement); the superRefine at `flow.zod.ts:1544` now hands the node but acts on `predicate` rows only (the new row is `value` → `continue`), and `found.block` is `'config'` for every predicate row, so the issue path is unchanged. **Right** — "Not narrowed" in the PR body holds.
7. **Published-surface widening (additive, rides the `minor`)** — new exports `FLOW_NODE_SIBLING_EXPRESSION_BLOCKS`, `FlowNodeExpressionBlock`, `FlowNodeSiblingExpressionBlock`, `FlowNodeSiblingBlocks`, `flowNodeExpressionBlock`, `getFlowNodeSiblingBlockJsonSchemas`; optional third parameter on `resolveFlowNodeExpressions`, `resolveFlowNodeValueSlots`, `flowNodeValueTemplateRefusals`; a `block` field on `ResolvedFlowNodeExpression` and `FlowNodeValueTemplateRefusal` (required on read; no constructor of either type exists outside `packages/spec`). `api-surface/automation.json` and `export-origins/automation.json` carry all six (check:generated green). **Right.** `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is the correct arm: the closed pair admits one arm and the narrowing is the BREAKING one; the additive exports are ordinary minor surface.
8. **Every prior ledger row resolves byte-identically** — `block` is optional, absent on all 21 earlier rows; the census test pins the 22-row order with the new row appended last; `entryRoot` returns `config` for a block-less row and the `root == null || typeof root !== 'object'` guard reproduces the old early return per row. **Right.**
9. **`flow-node-config-refusals.ts` excludes block-rooted rows** from `insideValueSlot` and `atOrInsideJudgedLedgerSlot`. Necessary and sufficient: without it `config.input` on a `connector_action` node would read as a judged value slot and shadow `siblingBlockLooseConfigRefusals`' loose-key refusal (`flow-sibling-block-loose-keys.ts`, `CONNECTOR_CONFIG_LOOSE_KEYS = ['connectorId','actionId','input']`). `slotJudgeRefusedPaths` (line 397) stays `config`-only, correctly: it dedupes config-contract issues against the config-rooted judges. **Right.**
10. **Ratchet third channel** — `getFlowNodeSiblingBlockJsonSchemas()` hands every non-`config` block; `declaredFromSiblingBlocks` fails on a marker in a block `FLOW_NODE_SIBLING_EXPRESSION_BLOCKS` does not name, and the keys are pinned to `['connectorConfig']`. The `.meta` on `z.unknown()` inside `z.record` survives `z.toJSONSchema` in `input` mode — proven by the ratchet's `['connector_action.connectorConfig.input.* (value)']` assertion under Test Core (green). **Right.**
11. **Producer-side amendments** — showcase `TaskCompletedSlackFlow` text → CEL envelope reading `record.title`; `record` is in scope (start node `record-after-update` on `showcase_task`). The other five in-tree inputs (connectors.mdx:434, preview-samples.ts:248, three showcase) are brace-free literals. The two DARK credential fixtures declare `api_token` as an input variable, so `{'clientSecret': api_token}` binds; the metadata-protocol gate (3/3) ran under Test Core. **Right**; the cli twin is unverified — ③/④.
12. **ADR-0087 disposition** — D3 entry `connector-action-input-value-slot-judged` at step 18 (spec is 18.2.0), Form D, no backticks in `surface`, `acceptanceCriteria` present, `reason` states why no D2 exists (no lossless token spelling; a malformed envelope carries no source to correct) — matches the ADR's "convert where lossless, a structured TODO otherwise". Marker `adr-0087: registered connector-action-input-value-slot-judged` on all three changesets (Check Changeset + Lint gates green). **Right.**

### ② Semver level

- Three changesets, `@objectstack/spec` / `@objectstack/service-automation` / `@objectstack/lint`, each `minor`, each carrying `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` line-initial, each with the BREAKING banner, the before/now, and the remedy (FROM → TO). AGENTS.md step 3: a kind other than `none` takes at least `minor` on a package the diff moves — `narrowed` ⇒ `minor` on all three. **Matches the diff.**
- `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` and `@objectstack/cli` are touched in test files only, `examples/app-showcase` is not a released package, `content/docs/references/automation/flow.mdx` is regenerated — none owes a changeset. **Matches.**
- Clause-②: `no (narrowing)` — one arm from the closed pair, BREAKING, present on the PR body and on every changeset. The declaration is true of the diff (①.1–3), not a false `no`. The additive exports (①.7) do not make it `yes`: the pair admits one arm and the narrowing governs.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Author: PR `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]` — no login note owed.
- `open_questions: []` in the os-dev-report — nothing to answer.
- Dev deviations (os-dev-report 6524784146), each answered:
  1. *File surface widened on the producer side* (showcase text, two DARK fixtures) — accepted; each is a consumer the new judge refuses, each rewrite preserves intent (①.11).
  2. *`packages/cli/test/flow-credential-literal-doors.e2e.test.ts` not run locally, "declared to CI"* — **not run anywhere on this head**: `*.e2e.test.*` is the nightly tier by name (`vitest-tiers.ts` header, `OS_TEST_TIERS` unset ⇒ nightly-tier files excluded), so the PR's Test Core did not collect it. Low risk (same fixture shape passed in metadata-protocol through the same lint pass) — carried as should-fix ④.4.
  3. *PR body prose* (two-vs-three skills files in 维护者速读; footer form) — prose face, the seat's; noted, not reviewed here.
  4. *Two merges of origin/main* — mechanical; the head's check-runs are the verdict.
- `Skills-docs:` line — present on the PR body as `Skills-docs: owed, left to a skills-lane edit (…)`, naming the three files. The pm-dispatch SKILL.md clause wants the closed form `follow-up owed — FILES` and the seat to file the card and rewrite it to `follow-up #N` before ACCEPT (review-checklist.md:18). Escalated to the seat as should-fix ④.1: the content is true (verified on the head: SKILL.md:88 and integration-recipes.md:18-21 state the retired limit; evals/integrations-declared.json:7 is not false, it already calls the input a value slot), the form is not the closed one.
- Check-runs on `6a06a420` (newest per name): every run is `success` or `skipped`; the skipped ones are opt-in harnesses, the matrix-template placeholders, the schedule gate and `Check PR Size` / `Auto Label` re-runs. No failure, no base-signature exception needed. Gate verdict: **green**.
- `auto_merge: null` — nothing to disarm. `needs:contract-review` is on the PR; a PASS record in the same hand removes it.

### ④ Design judgment

**packages/spec/src/automation/flow-node-expression-paths.ts** — the ruling's shape ("the ledger gains a way to address a node's sibling `connectorConfig` block, not a per-node special case") is met: `block` is a general optional root, `FLOW_NODE_SIBLING_EXPRESSION_BLOCKS` is the one table the ratchet and the resolvers both read, `entryRoot` is the single dispatch, and `waitEventConfig` is correctly left out (literals only). Tried to break it: a caller passing `config` only is answered for `config` only (test pins it); a loose `config.input` on a connector node is never read by the row (test pins it); `input` as an array yields nothing (the `*` walk refuses arrays); `onlyWithKey` would be read off the block, which is the right root. Holds. No finding.

**packages/spec/src/automation/flow-value-slot-template.ts** — the sibling-block branch takes the generic remedy and skips the callee/screen/recipient sentences; correct, since the connector was handed the token's text, not nothing (the three sentence suites now run through `refusalsForEntry` and still pin exactly the callee/screen/recipient rows). Holds. Observation, by ruling not a finding: this slot is the one value map most likely to carry provider-side brace syntax (a JSON-as-string body, GraphQL, mrkdwn), and `tokensOf` refuses every `{…}`, an `unresolvable` one included; the ruling forbids a connector-only judge, the in-tree survey found one hit, and the D3 entry declares the reach. Accepted as ruled.

**packages/spec/src/automation/flow-node-config-refusals.ts** — the two block filters are the exact two iterators that walk `config` positions; `slotJudgeRefusedPaths` correctly stays config-only. Holds. No finding.

**packages/spec/src/automation/flow.zod.ts** — the marker rides the block's own Zod, the value stays `z.unknown()`, the `describe` text and the example comment (rider from note 6518217696) now say what a value is; `getFlowNodeSiblingBlockJsonSchemas` is memoized and hands every non-`config` block so an unaddressable marker fails loudly. Holds. No finding.

**packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.connector-action-input-value-slot-judged.ts** — judged against its first consumer (the two doors) and the ADR: surface, reach (authoring, validate, authoring gate, boot), fate (skipped with warn; validate fails), remedy and the no-D2 reason are each true of the tree; the acceptance criteria name the printed locator string, which matches lint's `where` and registration's message byte for byte. Holds. No must-fix.

Findings (none must-fix):

1. **should-fix — governed skill text falsified at merge; `Skills-docs:` line not in the closed form.** `skills/objectstack-automation/SKILL.md:88` ("`os validate` does not judge it yet, so a malformed envelope fails at run time") and `references/integration-recipes.md:18-21` ("`{…}`, `{{ }}` are literal text … does not judge it yet") teach the limit this PR retires — and per ①.5 a `{{ }}` hole is refused there too, so an author following the recipe is refused by the door the recipe says is silent. Outside this card's claim (`skills/**`, skills lane), correctly declared; the seat files the skills-lane card and rewrites the line to `Skills-docs: follow-up #N` before ACCEPT, per pm-dispatch SKILL.md. Not a FAIL: the card's seam is ledger + two doors, both ends land here.
2. **should-fix — `packages/spec/src/conversions/refused-shapes.ts:406` detector `flow-value-slot-template-dialect-refused` walks `config` only** (`flowNodeValueTemplateRefusals(node.type, node.config)`, no node). Its header's invariant — "a site is listed here exactly when that door refuses it" — now has a hole: `os migrate meta --stored` will not name a stored `connector_action` row carrying a `{…}` token, although `registerFlow` refuses it at boot. The D3 entry compensates by naming the boot warn as the locator, so the operator has a path; the fix is one argument (hand the node) and a `connectorConfig` path prefix, reading the same ledger. File a card (noted in the PR, not filed).
3. **should-fix — Studio readers ignore `block`.** `flow-value-envelope.ts:isValueEnvelopeSlot` answers true for `['config','input']` on `connector_action` (unreachable: the parse refuses that loose key), and `FlowNodeConfigField.tsx:valueSlotRefusals` / `flow-simulator.ts:123` call the judge config-only — so the hand-written `connectorConfig` form offers no envelope editor and shows no refusal for a `{…}` token in `input`; the author meets it at the runtime authoring gate instead, located. Correct verdict, worse place. `ui/` lane card (noted in the PR, not filed).
4. **should-fix — `packages/cli/test/flow-credential-literal-doors.e2e.test.ts` amendment unverified on any run** (nightly tier by name; not in this PR's CI population; not run locally per the dev's own flag). Run it once (`vitest run --project integration` on that file, or the nightly) before or at landing; the same DARK envelope passed the same lint pass under metadata-protocol, so the expected outcome is green.

## 维护者速读
